neutral_facts.value: The accused assaulted the victim with weapons such as sticks, stones, and an axe, causing grievous injuries. The victim was taken to the hospital by the accused and others, where he later died. The prosecution witnesses, who were injured during the incident, provided detailed accounts of the assault and the weapons used. The victim was unconscious throughout the incident, and the delay in lodging the FIR was explained by the efforts to save his life. Medical evidence linked the injuries to the accused, establishing the cause of death as head injury with multiple injuries.

appeal_history.value: Trial court: Convicted A-1,2,3,4,7 & 10 under Section 302 r/w s. 149/PC; High Court: Confirmed conviction of A-1,2 & 7 under Section 302 r/w s. 34/PC, acquitted A-3,4 & 10; Supreme Court: Dismissed appeals, upheld conviction of A-1,2 & 7

quotes.text: The trial court convicted 6 out of 11 accused, namely, A-1, 2, 3, 4, 7 and 10 under Section 302 read with Section 149 of IPC and sentenced them to life imprisonment.

The High Court found A-1,2 and 7 guilty under Section 302 read with Section 34 of IPC and confirmed the sentence imposed upon them by the trial Court but acquitted A-3,4 and 10 by giving them the benefit of doubt.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused persons assaulted the deceased 'N' using weapons like axe, sticks, and stones, leading to his grievous injuries and eventual death. The witnesses PW-3, 4, and 5, who were relatives of the deceased, witnessed the incident and described the overt acts of the accused, particularly A-1, A-2, and A-7. The delay in lodging the FIR was explained by the fact that the deceased was taken to the hospital, and the lack of a dying declaration was justified as the deceased remained unconscious until death.

quotes.text: The prosecution case was that when 'N' came out of the house of PW-5, the accused persons who were sitting in the house of A-1 came out and they assaulted 'N' by means of axe, sticks and stones;
PWs 3, 4 and 5 not only witnessed the occurrence but also specified the overt acts of each accused, particularly, A-1, 2 and 7.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution's case should be disbelieved because the witnesses PW-3, 4, and 5 were relatives of the deceased, the delay in lodging the FIR was unexplained, no dying declaration was recorded, and the injuries sustained by some accused were not properly explained by the prosecution.

quotes.text: Merely because PW 3, 4 & 5 were related to the family of the victim, their testimonies cannot be eschewed
the delay in lodging of FIR cannot affect the prosecution case - Non-recording of dying declaration is inconsequential since the victim remained unconscious all throughout till his death

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the mere relationship of witnesses to the deceased does not invalidate their testimony, and that the prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt, especially when the witnesses are credible and their testimonies are corroborated by other evidence.

quotes.text: The entire prosecution rests on the evidence of PWs 3, 4 and 5. PW-3, who made the complaint to the police is brother of the deceased. Likewise, PW-4, who witnessed the occurrence is the son of the deceased and PW-5 is the mother-in-law of grand daughter of the deceased. But merely because the witnesses are related to the family of the deceased, their testimonies cannot be eschewed.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused assaulted the victim, inflicted multiple injuries, and shared a common intention to cause death, thereby satisfying the legal criteria for conviction under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the IPC.

quotes.text: The prosecution witnesses established that head injury was at the instance of A-7 and other injuries all over the body were at the instance of A-1 and A-2 by means of axe and sticks respectively.

Taking note of the same and the evidence of the doctor (PW-1) who conducted the post mortem, namely, the cause of death, it is clear that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt in respect of A-1 and A-2 (the appellants) and A-7 who assaulted the victim and inflicted multiple injuries and shared common intention.
